episodes.171019: Monsoon moisture increased across the region as the area of high pressure shifted towards the Southern Plains. The abundance of moisture fueled numerous showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. A debris flow occurred on the Pack Creek Fire burn scar as a result of a large amount of heavy rain in a short period of time which then flowed downstream to impact other areas such as near Moab which experienced some flash flooding. Additionally, thunderstorms produced damaging winds outside of Moab.
episodes.171084: The center of the upper-level high pressure remained centered over Colorado on August 11, 2022, while a weak disturbance raced northward through western New Mexico. This disturbance and plentiful moisture focused the greatest storm coverage for areas south of Interstate 40 with more isolated coverage north of Interstate 40. While many of these thunderstorms across the south were robust and capable of producing heavy rainfall, it was a thunderstorm on the Cerro Pelado burn scar in the Jemez Mountains that caused the only flash flooding report of the day.
episodes.171085: As the upper-level high pressure built over the Great Plains on August 12, 2022, much drier air pushed into eastern and central New Mexico. This led to a downtrend in thunderstorm coverage across much of the area while the monsoonal moisture plume focued across western New Mexico kept conditions relatively more active there. Despite this drier air, isolated thunderstorms were still able to form across the northern mountains although they were weak and short-lived. A rock slide was reported on Highway 68 southwest of Taos. While a thunderstorm did develop in this area and likely contributed to this rock slide, repeated rounds of heavy rain all monsoon season also likely contributed to this event.
episodes.171153: Some strong storms developed during the afternoon and evening hours, one of which became severe.
episodes.171182: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed along a frontal boundary and moved south into Lancaster Co SC.
episodes.171389: The combination of deep moisture and warm air along with forcing associated with an amplified trough across the eastern United States and a sea breeze circulation across southeast South Carolina led to a few thunderstorms producing damaging winds.
episodes.171448: The dry pattern finally changed to allow for several sea breeze showers and storms to develop ahead of a trough of tropical low pressure in the northwestern Gulf of Mexico. A few of these storms produced damaging winds and one storm produced a funnel cloud near La Joya on the evening of August 11th. Additional storms developed August 12th across more of the Rio Grande Valley/Deep South Texas region.  One storm became severe and produced damaging winds of 65 mph near the Mid Valley Airport in Weslaco.
episodes.171576: Heavy rainfall occurred over portions of the Mullen Fire Burn Scar area leading to evidence of debris flow in the backcountry wilderness during the afternoon of the 11th.
episodes.171725: An upper level trough on the West Coast slowly edged in between a ridge of high pressure to the east of the region. This allowed for monsoon moisture to move into the region along with strong southwest flow. Several days of isolated supercells occurred, bringing heavy rain and large hail to the region.
episodes.172094: A stalled cold front residing over the Central Appalachians was the main driver behind flash flooding that occurred between August 10th and 11th. The combination of slow moving and repetitive storms led to heavy downpours through the course of the day, before finally winding down that evening as the front began moving out of the area. 24 hour rainfall amounts reported by local observers and weather stations ranged from 1.5 to 3 inches in most places, with locally higher amounts on the upwards of 5 inches observed across north-central West Virginia.||Numerous roads across the northern half of the state became flooded, primarily during the afternoon when storms were at their strongest. This resulted in a few water rescues as vehicles became submerged by the inundating rainfall. Several homes in Ritchie County became surrounded by water for a period of time as well. The most significant damage transpired in Doddridge County, where the building of the local senior center was shoved five feet off of its foundation due to the deluge of water.
episodes.172923: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.173101: A shortwave passing across the region, combined with monsoonal flow and inverted V soundings, resulted in many severe wind gusts in the late afternoon/evening. A single severe hail report was received near Shelby.
episodes.173139: A surge of monsoon moisture along with an approaching upper level trough created an ideal environment for supercell thunderstorms across Clearwater and Idaho County.
episodes.173140: Modest instability, shear, and lift created an environment favorable for strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.173145: Sufficient shear, instability, moisture, and dry sub-cloud layer created an environment favorable for outflow winds.
episodes.173291: From August 11-14, thunderstorms produced gusty winds and localized flooding.
episodes.173341: In a classical monsoonal regime, with deep-layered east to southeast flow, high instability (MLCAPE in excess of 1000-1500 J/KG) along with abundant moisture (PWAT 1.8+ inches) resulted in an environment favorable for thunderstorms. An upper-level disturbance moving across Arizona, aided in increasing the areal coverage as well as enhancing the thunderstorm activity.
episodes.173359: The combination of deep moisture and warm air along with forcing associated with an amplified trough across the eastern United States led to thunderstorms producing damaging winds across coastal waters.
episodes.173413: A fairly typical summer-time air mass was in place on the 12th of August with abundant moisture throughout the atmospheric column and warm temperatures. As thunderstorms developed in the coastal waters, one was able to use increased low level moisture to intensify and produce a short-lived waterspout on Lake Ponchartrain.
episodes.173547: The active monsoon pattern continued over northern Arizona. A Flash Flood Watch was in effect from 11 AM MST to 11 PM MST in accordance with the Weather Prediction Center Excessive Rainfall Outlook (slight risk for northern Arizona).
episodes.173620: Thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona from late morning into early evening. Flash flooding occurred near Three Points and in Sabino and Bear Canyons where a large group of people became stranded. A dust storm rolled across Interstate 10 in Pinal County.
episodes.173663: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina foothills and Piedmont during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts across several counties.
episodes.173664: An isolated thunderstorm moving south into eastern York County from North Carolina produced locally damaging wind gusts and hail.
episodes.173701: As the slow moving Low continued through the region, another round of thunderstorms over the Eastern Washington produced large hail and strong winds to the region. The storms impacted extreme Eastern WA and the North ID Panhandle. Thunderstorms developed along an axis of instability stretching along the border between WA and ID.
episodes.173702: As the slow moving Low continued through the region, another round of thunderstorms over the Eastern Washington produced large hail and strong winds to the region. The storms impacted extreme Eastern WA and ID Panhandle. Thunderstorms developed along an axis of instability stretching along the border between WA and ID.
episodes.173706: A low pressure system off the WA coast continued to push weak waves of instability across Eastern WA. The instability was able to produce mid morning thunderstorms with large hail.
episodes.173707: A thunderstorm formed Southwest of Craigmont and moved Northeast. It collapsed over Craigmont. It brought strong winds and small hail.
episodes.173793: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173794: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.173795: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over southern Nevada. Several storms produced severe weather, and a few produced flash flooding.
episodes.173797: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Many storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173798: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.174004: Thunderstorm outflow winds were over 50 mph in Butte County.

events.narrative: Numerous trees were downed by strong winds in the east Kamiah area. Idaho Power and Light reported outages lasting 16 to 24 hours. In Kamiah, wind lifted a 40-foot wide roof into a neighbors yard.
Water and mud covered Goffs Road in multiple locations.

A strong storm developed in southern Hidalgo County and sagged to the southwest the evening of August 11th. At 7:08PM CDT, a member of the public began a Facebook Live that showed a funnel cloud dropping out of the storm. Radar analysis showed some mid-level rotation with the storm to corroborate the video and its timing. It dissipated by the end of the 2 minutes video, so around 7:10PM CDT.

Radar estimates of up to 2 inches of rainfall fell over a severely burned area of the Mullen Fire Burn Scar west and south of Rob Roy Reservoir. Evidence of debris flow with ash at A Bar A Ranch on the Mullen Creek.

High water was observed along West Virginia Avenue east of Clarksburg. A water rescue was conducted along Wilsonburg Road. In Mount Clare, Hoop Pole Hollow Road was flooded for a brief period of time.
Video shared by local broadcast media showed flooding and debris flow on the Cerro Pelado burn scar near Sierra de Los Pinos and the East Fork Jemez River. No damages are known.
Thunderstorm winds tore large sections of roofing and siding off a boat storage unit.
Strong winds downed trees, leading to an extended power outage in the Glenwood area.

A strong thunderstorm crossed over the WA, ID border near Stateline and tracked North to Hauser. It dropped hail ranging from half an inch to 2.75 inch. Most hail reports ranged from 0.75 inch to 1.5 inch. An estimated 2.75 inch size was reported around Hauser. Wind  also knocked down power lines near Carlin Bay airport.
Tree damage reported due to strong winds.
The Sundance Arrowhead mesonet weather station recorded a wind gust of 62 mph.

A strong thunderstorm dropped hail ranging from half an inch to 2.75. Most hail reports ranged from 0.75 to 1.5. A 2.75 size was reported around Newman Lake at 1700PST. It traveled from Albion WA to Newman Lake WA around 1525PST to 1715PST. It damaged at least 15000 acres of crops, broke windows and damaged siding of homes in Liberty Lake, and dented numerous vehicles.
A debris flow started on the Pack Creek Fire burn scar as measured by a USGS stream gauge which saw a notable jump as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms.

Several side streets and low lying areas flooded along Mill and Pack Creeks as a result of heavy rain over the Pack Creek Fire burn scar. Water ran out of its banks in many spots. The Mill Creek stream gauge in Moab increased by 9 feet in 2 hours. Additionally, areas near Moab reported 0.80 to 1.2 inches of rain.
Mud and rocks flowed across Desert Solitaire Road where it crosses Pack Creek as a result of heavy rain over the Pack Creek Fire burn scar.
Thunderstorm wind gusts estimated to be between 55-60 mph caused significant roof damage in the Navajo Ridge neighborhood outside Moab. Several solar panels were damaged.
Flash flooding occurred at the intersection of Pack Creek Road and La Sal Loop Road as a result of heavy rain over the Pack Creek Fire burn scar. Water pummeled the bridge and flowed over the road.

Trained spotter reported heavy rain from thunderstorms and measured 1.37 inches in less than an hour. Debris including mud and rocks flowed on nearby portions of Highway 191 in addition to some downed trees branches from strong winds.
Flash flooding occurred on Kane Springs Road as a result of heavy rain. Social media reports showed a prolific waterfall over slick rock.
Flash flooding occurred north-northwest of Moab as a result of heavy rain. Social media reports showed a prolific waterfall over slick rock with water flowing on the side of Utah Highway 128.
A swift water rescue was performed near mile post 40 on Alamo Road.

events.narrative: These gusts occurred at the North Las Vegas Airport and at Allegiant Stadium.

Heavy rain damaged classrooms, books, and electronics at Rose Warren Elementary School and poured through the roof of the Planet Hollywood casino. One man drowned in a wash near Giles St and Mandalay Bay Rd.

events.narrative: At roughly the same time, lightning from two different thunderstorm cores set trees on fire near Clayton and Washburn and also near Tenaya and Tropical.
A 60 mph thunderstorm outflow wind was measured at the INL Specific Manufacturing site.
A thunderstorm formed near Malden and moved Northeast near Plaza. It produced hail the size of half an inch to 1.5 inch.
A thunderstorm developed East of Connell and traveled North toward Ritzville. It produced  hail 1.5 inch in Lind WA around 0709PST. It also had reports of 0.75 inch and 1 inch.
Broadcast media relayed a video of a waterspout over Lake Ponchartrain near the Causeway at Mid Lake.
East County 14th Street in Yuma was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Social media pictures showed some tree damage in the form of broken branches and a damaged shed near the vicinity of 1st street and 20th Avenue in Yuma. Timing estimated from radar. Winds were estimated at around 45 mph. No injuries were reported.
The intersection of 4th Ave and 22nd St around the Post Office in Yuma was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Several reports of thunderstorm damage across Quartzsite. The damages reported included several trailers/RVs flipped, signs blown around, trees blown over, heavy grills thrown 50 feet, storage sheds destroyed, leaning power poles.  Timing estimated from radar. A wind gust of 65 mph was measured from a amateur radio user. No injuries were reported.
Heavy rain over the Pipeline, Tunnel, and Schultz fire scars caused flash flooding in the area that closed Highway 89 in both directions.
Tyson wash was reported to hit 12 feet deep with debris. No damages or injuries were reported.

A thunderstorm produced one inch diameter hail, heavy rain, and gusty winds (around 28 MPH).
The river gauge on Agua Fria measured a 5 foot rise in 15 minutes (starting at 1215 PM MST).

High flows were reported in the Clear Creek drainage in the southeastern portion of Zion National Park.

A pulse-severe thunderstorm produced a microburst with winds estimated at 65 mph across the northeast side of Weslaco.  Along its 2.3 mile track, damage included blown in siding at hangars at the airportand peeled back a metal roof on one of them.  Other damage included a small outbuilding that was flipped over, bent in fences, and a trampoline lifted and flung. The Mid Valley Airport ASOS in Weslaco officially recorded a 56 mph wind gust, but missed the core being about 300 meters west of the downburst.

Heavy rain of 2-3 at the headwaters of Sabino Creek and Bear Canyon caused rapid rises in both streams. Flash flooding occurred at the Sabino Canyon Recreation area causing damage to trails and flooding of all recreation area bridges. Twenty five people became stranded in Bear Canyon and needed to be rescued as trails across the wash were flowing heavily and dangerously impassable. No injuries were reported.
Multiple reports of hail ranging from 1-1.5 inches were submitted on social media.
Multiple trees and power lines were blown down in the city of Conover and power lines were blown down in Newton.
Sycamore Creek Road was closed from Burro Creek Crossing.
Burro Creek Crossing Road was closed from Highway 93 to mile marker 14.

Several roads in and near Golden Valley were closed, and one swift water rescue was performed.
